title:
Stroke in childhood due to inflammatory narrowing of blood vessels: 
Treatment with steroids
official:
High Dose Steroids in Children with Stroke and Unilateral Focal Arteriopathy:
A Multicentre Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Main objective: The purpose of this study is to evaluate if additional early anti-inflammatory treatment may influence the course of arteriopathy and improve clinical outcome and may prevent stroke recurrence in children with stroke and unilateral focal arteriopathy.
The primary objective of this study is to determine if a high dose course of methylprednisolone/prednisolone in addition to standard of care including antithrombotic treatment results in better improvement of focal arteriopathy in children with acute ischemic stroke and focal arteriopathy compared to standard of care alone.
conditions:
Focal cerebral arteriopathy and childhood stroke
Focal cerebral arteriopathy (FCA) is an inflammatory vessel wall disease
provoked by infection.

interventions.name: SOLUMEDROL 500 mg, poudre pour solution injectable

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Informed consent of the legal representative of the trial participant documented by signature
2. Age > 6 months & < 18 years at time of stroke
3. Randomisation possible within 48 hours of diagnosis and maximum 96 hours after stroke onset
4. Unilateral arteriopathy according to the following criteria:  •	Newly acquired neurologic deficits  •	Specific neuroimaging (MRA) features of either  -	unilateral stenosis, or  -	unilateral vessel irregularities within the CNS
5. Unless otherwise defined in the national addendum: Female participants age ≥ 13: Negative pregnancy test (blood or urine)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Previous stroke
2. Progressive large to medium childhood primary angiitis of the CNS (cPACNS ) with 2 of the following 3 criteria:  a.	pre-existing progressive neurocognitive dysfunction  b.	bilateral MRI lesions/vessel involvement  c.	small vessel arterial stenosis
3. On steroid treatment at disease onset
4. Contraindication to steroid treatment as e.g. a congenital or acquired immunodeficiency
5. Inability to follow the procedures of the study, e.g. due to language problems
6. Participation in another interventional study within the 30 days preceding the indication stroke and during the present study
7. Known syndromal disorders, as e.g. Trisomy 21, Neurofibromatosis type 1
8. Known genetic vasculopathies as e.g. PHACES syndrome, ACTA II
9. Moyamoya or sickle cell disease
10. Small vessel cerebral vasculitis (primary CNS vasculitis)
11. Bilateral arteriopathy
12. Arterial dissection(s)
13. Evidence of underlying systemic disorders, as e.g. lupus, rheumatoid problems
14. Secondary CNS angiitis due to infections (meningitis, endocarditis, borreliosis), or generalised angiitis due to rheumatic or other autoimmune problems
